1.title: Is It a Dog?
1.topic: a child on a foggy walk guesses shapes in the fog (a log, a van) until the last shape turns out to be Mom (weather, family, guessing game)
lines: Is it a *dog*? ↗ | *No*! It is a *big*, *wet* *log*. ↘
Is it a *man*? ↗ | *No*! It is a *tan* *van*. ↘
sounds: 입을 크게 벌리고 짧게 '아': dog '닥', log '락'. '도그', '로그'처럼 '오'로 읽지 않아요.
입을 옆으로 벌리고 '애': man '맨', van '밴', hat '햇'. '만', '반'이 되지 않게!
v는 윗니를 아랫입술에 살짝 대고 '브-' 떨리게: van. b는 두 입술을 붙였다 터뜨려요: big, bug.
1.expression: Say “Fog, fog!” slowly and softly like you are peeking, make every “Is it a…?” go up like a real guess, shout “No!” with a funny surprise, sound curious on “Who is that?”, be very surprised on “It is Mom!”, and end with a big, happy “Fun in the fog!”

2.title: Bubbles at Swim Class
2.topic: a girl is afraid to put her face in the water at her first swim class, and the coach's bubble-blowing game helps her go under step by step (sports, feelings, courage)
sounds: k·p·sh 뒤 -ed는 짧은 't': looked '룩트', dipped '딥트'. '룩키드'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
소리가 울리는 음 뒤 -ed는 'd': smiled '스마일드', tickled '티클드'.
2.expression: Sound a little scared on “held Mom's hand tight,” whisper “I don't want to put my face in,” use a warm, cheerful coach voice for “Let's play a game,” make bubbly sounds on “Blub, blub, blub!”, giggle on “It tickled!”, and shout “I did it!” with real pride.

3.title: Grandpa's First Text Message
3.topic: a girl patiently teaches her grandpa to use his new phone and send his first text message with a smiley face to her aunt (family, technology, patience, helping)
lines: *Grandpa* *Joe* has a *brand-new* *phone*, | but he *doesn't* *know* how to *use* it *yet*. ↘
“*Can* you *help* me, *Rosa*?” he *asks*. | “I *want* to *send* a *message* | to your *Aunt* *Lucy*.” ↘
*Rosa* *sits* *next* to him on the *couch*. | “*First*, | *tap* the *green* *bubble*,” she *says*. ↘
“*Now* *add* a *little* *picture*,” Rosa *says*. | Grandpa *picks* a *smiling* *face* | and a *slice* of *pie*. ↘
“*Tomorrow*, | will you *show* me | how to *take* a *picture*?” ↗
sounds: e·i 앞의 g는 'ㅈ' 소리가 나요: message '메시지', gently '젠틀리'. '메세게'가 아니에요.
s·z 소리로 끝나는 말에 -es가 붙으면 '이즈'가 한 음절 더: presses '프레시즈', buzzes '버지즈'.
couch는 '아우'를 미끄러지듯 한 번에: '카우치'. '코치'(coach)와 헷갈리지 않게!
3.expression: Use a slow, friendly old-man voice for Grandpa and a patient, cheerful voice for Rosa, sound surprised on “that the phone slides off his knee!”, giggle on “Gently, Grandpa!”, read “one letter at a time” very slowly, make “Whoosh!” fly away, sound happy on “Hi, Dad! Love you!”, and let Grandpa's last question rise hopefully.

4.title: The Big Winter Sleep
4.topic: hibernation: animals fatten up in fall, rest in burrows, logs or pond mud, and slow their bodies down; a woodchuck's heart drops from about 80 to 5 beats a minute, the wood frog freezes almost solid, and black bears sleep for months but wake more easily (animals, science, seasons)
lines: *Some* *animals* *fly* *south*. | *Others* *grow* *thick* *coats*. | But some animals *solve* the *problem* | in a *surprising* *way*: | they *sleep* *through* it! ↘
*Before* they *hibernate*, | many animals *eat* and *eat* | to *build* *up* a *layer* of *fat*. ↘
This *fat* *works* like a *packed* *lunch* | that their *bodies* will *use* | *all* *winter* *long*. ↘
*Then* they *find* a *safe* *place* to *rest*, | such as a *burrow*, | a *hollow* *log*, | or the *mud* at the *bottom* of a *pond*. ↘
A *woodchuck's* *heart* | *usually* *beats* about *eighty* *times* a *minute*. | In hibernation, | it may *beat* *only* *five* times! ↘
*What* about *bears*? ↗ | *Black* *bears* *sleep* for *months* in their *dens* | *without* *eating* or *drinking*, | but they can *wake* *up* *quickly* | if *something* *disturbs* them. ↘
sounds: hibernation은 'NA'에, surprising은 'PRIS'에 힘! burrow와 energy는 첫 음절, disturbs는 뒤 음절 'TURBS'에 힘을 줘요.
wake up, crawl out, thaws out, build up
앞 단어 끝소리를 뒤 모음에 이어서: wake up → '웨이컵', crawl out → '크롤라웃'. 끊지 말고 한 덩어리로!
4.expression: Open slowly and calmly like a nature narrator, pause before “they sleep through it!” and say it with a smile, slow your voice down on “an animal's body slows way down,” stress the big difference between “eighty times” and “only five times,” sound amazed on the wood frog's heart stopping, ask “What about bears?” with rising curiosity, and end warmly and thoughtfully.
practice: This long, deep rest is called hibernation.
nature's clever way of saving energy
